title: Founders of Agnikul Cosmos
content: Agnikul Cosmos was founded by Srinath Ravichandran, Moin SPM, Satyanarayanan Chakravarthy, and Janardhana Raju. Srinath Ravichandran is the Co-Founder and CEO, and Moin SPM is the Co-Founder and COO.
questions: Who is the CEO of Agnikul?

title: Agnikul Cosmos Founding Date
content: Agnikul Cosmos was founded on 1 December 2017 at IIT Madras through early academic incubation.

title: Agnikul Cosmos Headquarters
content: Agnikul Cosmos is headquartered in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India. The company is based in India and operates its development, testing, and launch-related activities within the country.

title: What Agnikul Cosmos Does
content: Agnikul Cosmos is an Indian private space technology company that focuses exclusively on building satellite launch vehicles. The company designs and manufactures orbital-class launch vehicles, specializing in fully customizable launch systems for small satellite missions. Agnikul does not design or manufacture satellites; its core mission is to provide reliable and flexible launch solutions.

title: Agnikul Cosmos Industry
content: Agnikul Cosmos operates in the aerospace and space transportation industry, with a specific focus on launch vehicle design, manufacturing, and orbital launch services for small satellites.
questions: What sector does Agnikul work in?

title: Agnikul Cosmos Tagline
content: The tagline of Agnikul Cosmos is 'Launch anywhere, anytime, affordably.' This reflects the company's focus on flexible launch locations, rapid readiness, and cost-effective access to space.
questions: What is the tagline of Agnikul?

title: Agnibaan Launch Vehicle
content: Agnibaan is the primary orbital-class launch vehicle developed by Agnikul Cosmos. It is designed to launch small satellites into orbit and represents the company's core product offering in space transportation. Agnibaan enables dedicated satellite launches with customizable mission configurations.
questions: What launch vehicle does Agnikul build?

title: Agnilet Rocket Engine
content: Agnilet is a semi-cryogenic rocket engine developed by Agnikul Cosmos. It produces approximately 6.2 kilonewtons of thrust and uses liquid oxygen and kerosene as propellants. Agnilet is manufactured using high-performance Inconel alloys and is a fully indigenous engine powering Agnikul's launch vehicle. It is a single-piece 3D-printed rocket engine.

title: Semi-Cryogenic Fuel System
content: A semi-cryogenic fuel system uses liquid oxygen as the oxidizer and refined kerosene as the fuel. It offers higher thrust, better efficiency, and easier handling compared to fully cryogenic systems. Liquid oxygen provides high performance and improves combustion efficiency. Kerosene is easier to store and handle than cryogenic fuels like liquid hydrogen. Semi-cryogenic engines are commonly used in the first stage of launch vehicles.

title: Dhanush Mobile Launch Pedestal
content: Dhanush is Agnikul Cosmos's private mobile launch pedestal, designed to support flexible launch operations and align with the company's goal of launching from adaptable locations. It enables the 'Launch anywhere' capability mentioned in the tagline.
questions: What is the mobile launch pedestal?
What is Agnikul's mobile launch pedestal?

title: Agnibaan SOrTeD
content: Agnibaan SOrTeD is a suborbital technology demonstrator used to validate systems before full orbital missions. SOrTeD is a sub-orbital launch vehicle developed by Agnikul Cosmos, designed to carry payloads of up to approximately 30 kilograms to near-space. It includes avionics systems, composite structures, propellant tanks, fins, and a 3D-printed engine base.

questions: Can I add multiple PPE items in one safety request?
Where do I enter PPE quantity and size?

title: Safety Dashboard and Request Tracking
content: The Safety Dashboard provides an overall summary of safety requests, including counts for pending, approved, rejected, permitted, and completed requests. Charts display work status distribution, request types, and new versus extension requests, with filters for date range analysis.
questions: Where can I see an overall summary of safety requests?
How do I know how many safety requests are pending?

title: Reporting and Managing Non-Conformance
content: A non-conformance is raised when a deviation from an approved procedure or expected quality outcome is identified. The record includes issue details, severity, internal or external classification, corrective actions, preventive actions, and status tracking until resolution or closure.
questions: What kind of issues can be reported as non-conformance?
What happens after I raise a quality non-conformance?

title: Reporting Damaged Materials or Parts
content: Damaged materials are reported using a damage report. Multiple affected parts can be listed in one report, each with condition notes such as repairable, damaged, or unusable. Attachments like photos can be added, and the report status shows progress until completion.
questions: How do I report damaged materials?
Can I report multiple damaged parts in one report?

title: Raising and Tracking Inspection Requests
content: Inspection requests are raised for inward materials, components, or calibration needs. Supporting documents such as supplier delivery notes can be attached. Inspection outcomes include cleared, not cleared, rejected, or inspection not required, based on quality review.
questions: What outcomes can an inspection request have?
How do I request an inspection for received materials?

title: Quality Request Status and Assignment
content: Quality requests move through statuses such as pending, approved, in progress, completed, or rejected. When a request is assigned, it indicates a quality team member is responsible for reviewing or executing the task. Progress and remarks are visible in the request record.
questions: What does in progress mean for a quality request?
How do I know if someone is working on my quality request?

title: Creating and Managing Projects
content: Projects are created in the Task Management application by entering project name, members, start date, end date, description, and project lead. All tasks related to the project are tracked under the project record.
questions: How do I create a new project?
What details are required while creating a project?

title: Creating, Updating, and Completing Tasks
content: Tasks are created by specifying task name, assigned user, due date, and linked project. Task statuses include todo, in progress, overdue, and completed. Users update status, add notes, and mark tasks as completed once work is finished.
questions: How do I create and update a task?
What task status options are available?

title: Logging and Reviewing Time Spent on Tasks
content: Time spent on tasks is recorded using time logs by entering start time, end time, and optional notes. Time logs can be added later if missed and are used to review work duration and effort across tasks.
questions: How do I log time spent on a task?
Can I add time logs later?

title: Purpose of Feedback Templates in Quality
content: A feedback template defines the parameters that need to be evaluated during a quality feedback activity. Selecting a template ensures that ratings are captured consistently against predefined criteria, making feedback comparable and structured.
questions: Why do I need to select a feedback template?
What is the role of a feedback template in quality?

title: Meaning of Ratings in Quality Feedback
content: Ratings in quality feedback represent how well each defined parameter met the expected standards or requirements. They provide a measurable way to assess performance or outcomes during quality activities.
questions: What do the ratings in quality feedback represent?
How are ratings used in quality feedback?

title: Quality Goals and Their Review
content: Quality goals define targets that guide daily work and continuous improvement. These goals are periodically reviewed, and each review is recorded with outcomes to track progress over time.
questions: How are quality goals used in daily work?
How do I know when a quality goal is reviewed?

title: Quality Meetings and Minutes
content: Quality meetings record discussion points as meeting minutes. Each meeting has a status that indicates whether it is open or closed, helping teams track pending discussions and completed reviews.
questions: Where are quality meeting discussions recorded?
How do I know if a quality meeting is still open?

title: Understanding Quality Procedures
content: Quality procedures describe the steps required to perform a process correctly. Sub-processes or sub-steps are listed under the main procedure details, helping users understand the complete workflow before starting work.
questions: How do I understand a quality procedure before starting work?
How do I know if a procedure has sub-steps?

title: Getting Started in Quality Management
content: New users should start by reviewing relevant quality procedures and checking active requests or assignments. The Quality Management page allows users to raise new requests, track existing ones, and review non-conformance records.
questions: I’m new to the quality process, where should I start?
What can I do first in Quality Management?

title: Tracking Quality Requests and Assignments
content: Quality requests can be tracked using the Track Request view, which shows current status such as pending, approved, or in progress. The Assignments section lists quality tasks assigned to a user, including inspection-related work.
questions: How do I check the status of my quality request?
Where can I see quality work assigned to me?

title: Raising and Closing Non-Conformance
content: Non-conformance records are used to report deviations from expected quality, process issues, or material defects. A record remains open until corrective actions are completed and verified, after which it can be closed.
questions: What issues should be raised as non-conformance?
When should a non-conformance be marked as closed?

title: Meaning of Quality Request Statuses
content: A pending status means the request has been submitted and is awaiting review or action. In progress indicates the quality team is actively working on the request. Assignment details show who is responsible for handling it.
questions: What does pending mean for a quality request?
What does in progress indicate in quality?

title: Raising a Material Request
content: Material requests are raised from the Inventory module by specifying whether the request is for a project or department, the purpose, location, and required items. Items are added with quantity and tracking type details.
questions: How do I raise a material request?
What details are needed for a material request?

title: Item Tracking Types in Material Requests
content: Tracking type defines how an item is managed in inventory. Items can be tracked by serial number, batch number, as fixed assets, or treated as consumables, depending on their nature and usage.
questions: What does tracking type mean in a material request?
What are the different item tracking types?

title: Material Request Status and Receipt
content: A pending material request is awaiting assignment or action. To-Receive indicates material is ready to be received. After receiving items, the requester must acknowledge receipt so the request can move toward completion.
questions: What does pending mean in a material request?
What should I do after receiving material?

title: Reporting Damaged or Returnable Items
content: Damaged items are recorded in the damage item log within the material request. Details include damaged quantity, batch or serial number, and remarks. Returnable items must be logged as returned to update their status correctly.
questions: What should I do if the received item is damaged?
How do I return a returnable item?

title: Batch Ledger and Stock Movement
content: The batch ledger shows batch-wise stock movement. Transaction type IN indicates stock addition, while OUT indicates stock issued or moved out. Available quantity for a batch is visible in the ledger record.
questions: What does IN or OUT mean in batch ledger?
Where can I see available quantity for a batch?

title: Material Inward and Inspection
content: Material inward is recorded using the Material Inward Log, capturing vendor details, inward date and time, and reference documents. IIR pending indicates inspection is required and not yet completed. Inspection Not Required means no inspection is needed.
questions: How is material inward recorded in ERP?

title: Checking Completion of Inventory Tasks
content: An inventory task is considered completed when the related material request or assignment shows a status of Completed. Users should check the overall status of the material request or the specific assignment record to confirm completion.
questions: How do I check if my inventory task is completed?
How do I know my inventory request is fully done?

title: Checking Material Availability Before Request
content: Material availability can be checked before raising a request by reviewing recent item or batch movements in Inventory. Batch ledgers and item movement history help determine whether sufficient stock is available.
questions: How do I know if an item is available before raising a request?
Where can I check stock availability?

title: Material Allocation and Issuance
content: Allocated quantity refers to material reserved for a request but not yet issued. Allocation depends on stock availability and may be partial if full quantity is unavailable. Materials can be issued from one or multiple warehouses as required.
questions: Why is my requested quantity higher than allocated quantity?

title: Receiving and Returning Materials
content: Once materials are issued, the request status changes to To-Receive. The assigned person can acknowledge receipt. Unused materials can be returned fully or partially using the return section of the original request, and statuses update accordingly.
questions: How will I know when material is ready for receipt?
Can I partially return issued items?

title: Reporting and Handling Damaged Materials
content: Any damaged material must be logged using the damage item log in the material request. Damaged items can still be returned but are marked separately. Damage reporting is mandatory to maintain accurate inventory records.
questions: How do I report material damage?

title: Tracking Materials Using Transactions
content: Inventory transactions track material movement. IN indicates stock added, OUT indicates stock issued, TRANSFER shows movement between locations, RETURN represents returned items, and DAMAGE marks unusable stock removed from availability.
questions: What do different transaction types mean in inventory?

title: Material Inward and Inspection Status
content: Material inward records capture receipt from vendors along with documents and values. IIR Pending means inspection is required and not completed. IIR Cleared indicates inspection approval, while Inspection Not Required means material can be used without inspection.

title: Cancelling Inventory Requests
content: Inventory requests can be cancelled if they have not been processed. When a request is cancelled, any allocated quantities are released back into available stock automatically.
questions: Can an inventory request be cancelled?
What happens to allocated items after cancellation?

title: Office Beverage Availability
content: Tea, Coffee, Milk, and Biscuits are available across all facilities on all working days except Sunday. Beverage availability is uniform across locations and does not require individual booking.
questions: What beverages are available in the office?

title: Food Booking and Consumption Process

questions: How do I book food in the ERP?
How is food marked as consumed?

title: Food Log and Meal Status
content: The Food Log displays booked meals, consumption status, scan time, and location. Status values include Not Booked, Not Consumed, and Consumed. Only Breakfast, Lunch, and Dinner appear in the Food Log.
questions: What does Not Consumed status mean?
Where can I see my food consumption history?

title: Food Availability and Location Rules
content: Food availability is managed location-wise, and users must select the correct location while booking. Booking may be limited if availability is exhausted, and booking windows define when meals can be booked or modified.
questions: Does location matter while booking food?
How do I know if booking is closed for a meal?

title: Food Booking Window Rules
content: Food booking is allowed only within the defined booking window. Once the booking end time closes, users cannot book meals for that meal slot. This rule applies uniformly to Breakfast, Lunch, and Dinner.
questions: Can I book food after the booking end time?
Why can’t I book food now?

title: Dinner Booking and Consumption Process
content: Dinner booking follows the same rules as Breakfast and Lunch. Users must book the meal within the booking window and scan the QR code before consuming food for it to be marked as consumed.
questions: Is dinner booking handled the same way as lunch?
How is dinner marked as consumed?

title: Dietary Preference in Food Booking
content: Dietary preference is displayed in the booking preferences section for reference. However, food booking is always done by meal type only and is not restricted or changed based on dietary preference.
questions: Does dietary preference affect food booking?
Where can I see my dietary preference?

title: Accuracy of Food Consumption Data
content: Food consumption data is recorded accurately based on two conditions: the meal must be booked, and the QR code must be scanned before consumption. The Food Log updates immediately after a successful QR scan.
questions: How accurate is food consumption data?
Does the food log update immediately?

title: QR Code Rules for Food Consumption
content: QR scanning is mandatory to mark a booked meal as consumed. The scan must be done by the employee consuming the food and before eating. Consumption without booking or QR scanning is not recorded.
questions: Why is QR scanning required for food?
Can someone else scan the QR code for me?

content: The Food Log shows booked meals, consumption status, scan time, and location. Status values include Not Booked, Not Consumed, Consumed, and Consumed Not Booked, which indicates an attempted consumption without a valid booking.
questions: What does Consumed Not Booked mean?
Can I see a summary of my food usage?

content: Only Breakfast, Lunch, and Dinner consumption is recorded in the Food Log. Snacks and beverages do not appear in the log.

content: If you booked lunch but did not eat it, the meal will appear as not consumed in the Food Log. This indicates booking without consumption confirmation.

content: Food cannot be marked as consumed without booking. Only booked meals can be recorded as consumed in the system.

content: If you consume food without booking it, the system will not record it as consumed. Booking is a prerequisite for consumption tracking.

content: Meal cancellation depends on the booking window rules set in the Food application. Not all bookings can be cancelled.

content: Location changes depend on whether booking modification is still allowed. Some changes may not be permitted after booking.

content: The Food application shows booking end time for each meal. You can see when the booking window closes.

content: You cannot book food after the booking window closes. Booking is not allowed once the deadline passes.
